data_description.kind: Choose GPS location, Home Wi-Fi connection, Home BLE presence, or room detection.

data_description.attribute: For Wi-Fi, BLE and room signals, leave blank to read the entity state, or enter an attribute such as ssid. GPS always uses latitude, longitude and gps_accuracy.
data_description.positive: For Wi-Fi/BLE only. Enter one exact value per line, such as on or home. For an SSID sensor, enter only your Home network name. Matching is case-sensitive.
data_description.negative: For Wi-Fi, BLE and room signals. Enter one exact Away value per line, such as off or not_home. Unlisted Wi-Fi/BLE values remain unknown; room signals use other known values as room names.
data_description.freshness: For Wi-Fi, BLE and room signals, use expiry handled by the source integration, or a reliable measurement/heartbeat timestamp plus a validity period.
data_description.timestamp_attribute: Enter the attribute holding the actual measurement or heartbeat time. Required for timestamp-based expiry. For GPS, leaving it blank counts only coordinate/accuracy changes as new measurements.
data_description.timestamp_format: Match the timestamp attribute: ISO 8601 with a timezone, Unix seconds, or Unix milliseconds. Units are not detected automatically.
data_description.ttl: Used only for timestamp-based local expiry. Enter 1–86400 seconds; after this time the signal becomes unknown. GPS has a separate expiry setting.
data_description.room_mapping: For room signals, enter one source=display name per line, such as bedroom=Bedroom. Unlisted names are unchanged.

data_description.movement_window_s: Retain measured path contributions within this many seconds.
data_description.movement_bucket_s: Group measurements into intervals aligned to UTC. Keep the most accurate measurement in each interval, or the newest on a tie. Must be shorter than the movement history window.
data_description.minimum_movement_m: Minimum measured path in metres before becoming a movement challenger.
data_description.gps_stale_after_s: Seconds since measurement before automatic GPS use stops.
data_description.gps_fresh_full_s: Seconds before the freshness score begins to decrease; below GPS expiry.
data_description.gps_max_accuracy_m: Reject automatic candidates with reported accuracy worse than this many metres.
data_description.gps_missing_accuracy_m: Conservative metres when accuracy is absent/invalid; assumed values cannot confirm reunion.
data_description.gps_future_tolerance_s: Maximum accepted measurement clock lead in seconds.
data_description.max_observation_gap_s: Do not connect path segments across larger gaps in seconds.
data_description.max_speed_m_s: Accuracy-adjusted metres/second limit; not a guarantee for air travel.
data_description.pair_max_skew_s: Maximum measurement time difference in seconds for pair comparisons.
data_description.pair_max_age_s: Maximum age in seconds of each position used for grouping.
data_description.together_radius_m: Distance plus both accuracy values must be within this many metres.
data_description.separation_radius_m: Distance minus both accuracy values must exceed this many metres; above together radius.
data_description.group_confirm_s: Minimum span in seconds of at least three new close observations.
data_description.challenger_ratio: Candidate score must strictly exceed primary score multiplied by this ratio.
data_description.challenger_margin: Candidate score must also strictly exceed primary score plus this margin.
data_description.challenger_hold_s: Seconds of continuous score advantage before switching.
data_description.minimum_primary_hold_s: Minimum seconds before ordinary switches; departure/failover have separate rules.
data_description.reunion_hold_s: Seconds of renewed observations with previously separated devices.
data_description.safe_companion_age_s: Maximum seconds since confirmed companionship to authorize failover.
data_description.home_enter_hold_s: Seconds of eligible local home evidence before entering home.
data_description.gps_home_enter_hold_s: The GPS position and its accuracy circle must remain inside the selected Home boundary for this long. Uses the HA Home circle unless a GeoJSON area set is selected.
data_description.home_exit_hold_s: Seconds of valid GPS outside home before leaving home.
data_description.home_exit_margin_m: Require this extra distance beyond the selected Home boundary, in addition to GPS error, before confirming departure.
data_description.nearby_enter_m: Distance from the HA Home center. Must exceed the Home radius, or the distance to the furthest Home polygon vertex.
data_description.nearby_exit_m: Metres from Home centre to leave nearby; must exceed entry distance.
data_description.direction_window_s: Seconds of same-source continuous path used for direction.
data_description.direction_min_span_s: Minimum observed span in seconds, with at least three positions.
data_description.direction_min_change_m: Minimum change in Home distance in metres, also guarded by accuracy.
data_description.direction_slope_m_s: Absolute regression slope in metres/second required for towards or away_from.
data_description.room_change_hold_s: Seconds of a stable room name before changing the output.
data_description.room_missing_hold_s: Maximum seconds to retain a room after its source disappears.
data_description.evidence_hold_s: Maximum seconds of held presence; then unknown, never inferred away.
data_description.manual_override_default_s: Default override seconds from 1 to 86400; expiry is not extended on restart.

This recipe generates editable Jinja; it does not configure your Matter bridge. Choose source categories, your own measurement boundaries, a fixed category, or custom Jinja. A categorical sensor.name_air_quality companion is generated on the same Device for MatterBridge 3.10.8 + matterbridge-hass 1.5.0. Existing virtual sensors receive it on reload too. Original sensors are unchanged. A sensor.object_id_aqim compatibility mirror is also generated for matterbridge-hass 1.5.0; match that ID in the bridge's Air Quality Regex.

data_description.device_name: Display name only. Different Devices may use the same name; Device ID determines grouping.

data_description.entity_id: Optional. Defaults to domain.entity_name using the virtual entity name with abbreviations; the Device name is not included. An unnamed form leaves this blank. Clear to regenerate from the current name, or enter your own ID. Saved IDs are preserved when names change.

data_description.initial_availability: Initial availability used when no availability template is configured.
data_description.persistent: Restore the last state after Home Assistant restarts. Disable it to return to the initial value. Air-quality grades always retain their last valid result during outages and restart; air_quality_stale marks retained readings.
data_description.value_template: Jinja template for the main entity state. Copying source entities generates a helper; an edited custom template is preserved during later source changes.
data_description.availability_template: Optional Jinja template that returns whether the virtual entity is available. Example expression (wrap it in Jinja delimiters): states("sensor.gateway") not in ["unknown", "unavailable"] and is_state("input_boolean.enabled", "on")
data_description.source_entities_text: Comma-separated or one entity ID per line. Changes trigger template updates.
data_description.pull_interval: Seconds between periodic source checks. Use 0 to update only on source state changes.

device_details.name: Device details
device_details.description: Optional Home Assistant device registry metadata. Existing devices can also be maintained from Manage Devices.

data_description.device_id: The sole stable identifier used for Device grouping and the Home Assistant device registry. Leave empty to generate one.
data_description.device_manufacturer: Optional manufacturer shown in the Home Assistant device registry.
data_description.device_model: Optional model shown in the Home Assistant device registry.
data_description.device_sw_version: Optional software version shown in the Home Assistant device registry.
data_description.device_hw_version: Optional hardware version shown in the Home Assistant device registry.
data_description.device_serial_number: Optional serial number shown in the Home Assistant device registry.

advanced_settings.name: Advanced settings
advanced_settings.description: Optional source mappings, attributes, event hooks, command actions, and integration-specific settings.

data_description.template_sources_json:
Maps Jinja variable names to source states or attributes. YAML example:
source: sensor.room_temperature
battery: sensor.remote.battery_level
Use variables named source and battery in editable templates.
Multiple sources:
source: sensor.room_temperature
battery: sensor.remote.battery_level
Then reference the variables from value_template.
data_description.event_hooks_json:
Runs editable helpers after a state or event trigger. YAML example:
- trigger: state
  entity_id: [sensor.source]
  value_template: trigger.to_state.state  # wrap in Jinja delimiters
Hooks may also set availability_template, attributes, and attribute_templates.
data_description.attributes_json:
Static extra attributes published by the virtual entity. YAML example:
source_type: composite
priority: 1
data_description.attribute_sources_json:
Maps a virtual attribute to a real entity state or attribute. YAML example:
battery: sensor.remote.battery_level
mode: select.real_mode.state
data_description.attribute_templates_json:
Maps attributes to editable Jinja helpers. YAML example:
power: states("sensor.power") | float(0)  # wrap this expression in Jinja delimiters
Automatic helpers use boolean AND/OR, numeric average, unique list union, string concatenation, or ordered mapping merge according to value type.
data_description.native_templates_json:
Maps native Home Assistant properties to Jinja. YAML example:
vendor_property: state_attr("sensor.source", "vendor_property")  # wrap in Jinja delimiters
Managed properties are normally shown individually in Native values; this editor keeps additional domain/vendor properties editable.
data_description.command_actions_json:
Maps every virtual-domain command to Home Assistant actions. Command arguments such as preset_mode, percentage, temperature, option, or position are template variables. YAML example:
set_preset_mode:
  - choose:
      - conditions: preset_mode == "sleep"  # wrap in Jinja delimiters
        sequence:
          - action: input_select.select_option
            target:
              entity_id: input_select.real_mode
            data:
              option: quiet
A value may be one action, an action list, or a mapping with sequence and optimistic keys.
More examples:
turn_on:
  - action: switch.turn_on
    target:
      entity_id: switch.real_device
set_percentage:
  - action: number.set_value
    target:
      entity_id: number.fan_speed
    data:
      value: percentage # command variable; wrap expressions in Jinja delimiters
data_description.domain_options_json:
Additional selected-domain options not represented by dedicated inputs. YAML example:
source_entity: camera.front_door
stream_source: rtsp://example/stream
Reserved common fields cannot be overridden.
Climate example:
hvac_modes: select.climate_modes
current_temperature: sensor.room_temperature
Fan example:
preset_modes: select.fan_modes
Use dedicated Native values for standard properties when available.

data.air_quality_per_source: Create one air-quality sensor per source

data_description.polygon_geojson_json: Optional GeoJSON FeatureCollection containing named Polygon or MultiPolygon features. Used only by device_tracker entities.
data_description.polygon_files_text: One local path or HTTP(S) GeoJSON URL per line. Relative paths are resolved below the Home Assistant configuration directory.
data_description.polygon_person: Optional person represented by this virtual tracker. The configured source trackers determine the map position.
data_description.polygon_strategy: Adaptive follows observed movement, checks GPS accuracy and speed, and keeps the carried device during stops; stale positions are marked. Majority groups nearby trackers, priority selects the lowest rule priority, latest uses the newest update, and median combines all valid positions. Dominant rules override adaptive selection.
data_description.polygon_distance_meters: Distance in meters for majority grouping, or for adaptive handoffs and unconfirmed outlier selection.
data_description.polygon_tracker_rules_json: Optional object keyed by tracker entity ID. Rules support dominant, weight, priority, max_age_seconds, max_gps_accuracy, enabled, and condition_template.
data_description.polygon_espresense_anchors_json: Anchor map keyed by ESPresense distance sensor. Each anchor needs latitude and longitude; three or more valid distances are triangulated and resolved through the GeoJSON zones.
data_description.polygon_away_state: State used when the selected GPS position is outside every polygon.
data_description.presence_classification: When enabled for a combined tracker, Wi-Fi/ESPresense presence is home; BLE distance is front_door; GPS distance from zone.home becomes near_home, away, or far_away.
data_description.matter_light_type: Choose the maximum virtual-light capability: on/off, dimming, color temperature, or extended HS/XY color. When combining bulbs, the generated helper uses the least capable profile: RGB plus color-temperature becomes color temperature, and any on/off-only bulb makes the virtual light on/off only. Effects and flash are never exposed.
data_description.light_response_delay: Seconds to retain a requested light value before reading source states again (0–30).
data_description.light_response_retries: For light groups, refresh source devices and resend the latest command only to bulbs that have not reached the target (0–10 retries). A new command cancels old retries. Single-source lights only re-read state.
data_description.light_ignore_unresponsive: Keep the combined light available and use responding bulbs when another selected bulb is unavailable.
data_description.sensor_unit: Choose a normalized Home Assistant unit to replace the unit template. Keep template preserves dynamic or custom units. This does not convert readings.
data_description.utility_meter_enabled: Accumulate one source sensor as a Utility Meter. This creates a period total and follows source increases; source resets are ignored.
data_description.boiler_dynamic_control: Opt in for one boiler and room sensors in Celsius. Replaces the configured set_temperature action with periodic water-temperature writes. Set a room target after enabling. Calculates every 60s; writes at least 120s apart. Boiler current_temperature must measure heating water. Power actions remain separately configured.
data_description.boiler_dynamic_template: Returns Celsius. Variables: temperature (saved room target), room_temperature (sensor mean), boiler_water_temperature, room_temperature_rate (C/min over up to 10min), heating_elapsed_minutes (observed heat duration), heat_accumulation (decaying C-min proxy, 30min time constant), base_water_temperature (existing calibration result). Tune default gains for the system. Missing inputs pause writes. Boiler limits and steps apply.
data_description.boiler_room_temperature_entity_id: Optional sensors combined as the virtual climate's current room temperature. Available numeric readings are averaged; raw boiler-water temperatures remain available as attributes.
data_description.media_player_source_priority: Optional ordered fallback for the combined player. Drag sources into priority order. A playing, paused, or buffering source wins first; off, idle, unavailable, or unusable sources fall through. This shared order applies to all standard media-player properties.
data_description.onvif_patrol_enabled: Starts the patrol after this virtual camera loads. The video source remains independent from the PTZ target.
data_description.onvif_patrol_target: Select the camera created by Home Assistant's existing ONVIF integration. Its authenticated ONVIF client is also used if the PTZ action is unavailable.
data_description.onvif_patrol_mode: Legacy relative patrol only: horizontal alternates left/right, vertical down/up, grid both axes. A saved route from Configure camera patrol positions takes priority over these axes and ranges.
data_description.onvif_patrol_interval: Seconds to wait after each relative ONVIF move.
data_description.onvif_patrol_speed: Optional ONVIF speed coefficient, from 0 to 1.
data_description.onvif_patrol_pan_min: Relative move distance from 0 to 1 for each left movement.
data_description.onvif_patrol_pan_max: Relative move distance from 0 to 1 for each right movement.
data_description.onvif_patrol_tilt_min: Relative move distance from 0 to 1 for each down movement.
data_description.onvif_patrol_tilt_max: Relative move distance from 0 to 1 for each up movement.
data_description.patrol_auto_cycle: Start patrol on load, then repeat on/off periods. Manual patrol switch or service control suspends automatic cycles until reload.
data_description.patrol_on_seconds: How long each automatic patrol session runs. Default 300 seconds.
data_description.patrol_off_seconds: Time between the end of a session and the next start, after cleanup. Default 1800 seconds.
data_description.patrol_recording_scope: Apply recording policy for the entire patrol, or only during each movement including return. Between moves the previous state is restored.
data_description.patrol_settle_seconds: Wait this long after movement, then send ONVIF Stop before restoring recording. This is a timing estimate, not position feedback; increase for slower cameras.
data_description.frigate_recording_switch: Optional: select the Frigate recording switch. Otherwise controls are discovered on the source camera’s Frigate device. No other camera is controlled.
data_description.frigate_mqtt_recordings_topic: Base topic such as frigate/front/recordings. Also controls sibling detect and motion topics. Leave the switch empty. Requires state confirmation before movement.
data_description.frigate_recording_during_patrol: Off (default) disables recording during the selected control period. On enables it; Keep leaves it unchanged. Configure detection separately below. Stop restores the prior state.
data_description.frigate_motion_during_patrol: Controls both detect and motion. Off disables detection before motion; On enables motion before detection. Keep preserves both. Set both recording and detection to Off for quiet patrol.
data_description.configure_air_quality_rules: Automatically classify recognized PM1.0, PM2.5, PM4, PM10, radon, formaldehyde, CO2, CO, NO2, ozone, SO2, NO, N2O, benzene, ammonia, hydrogen sulfide and TVOC/eTVOC (mass or parts) measurements with separate starter profiles, then use the worst available grade. Source categories and AQI are also supported. Unsupported quantities or units remain unknown. Display bands are instantaneous, not official health standards or exposure-time assessments; good does not certify safe air. dawarich_settings.description: Read location and history from Dawarich.

data.dawarich_member: Family member email or user ID

data_description.dawarich_enabled: Enable polling for this tracker. Turn off to remove its saved Dawarich configuration.
data_description.dawarich_url: Base URL without /api/v1, for example https://dawarich.example.com.
data_description.dawarich_api_key: Stored in this integration configuration. The password field hides it on screen; it is not published in entity attributes.
data_description.dawarich_auth_mode: Use Bearer token or api_key query-parameter authentication.
data_description.dawarich_poll_interval: Seconds between API polls (15–3600). Point freshness uses its measurement timestamp, not poll time.
data_description.dawarich_history_limit: Maximum recent location summaries retained in dawarich_history (1–100). Family mode returns only the current location.
data_description.dawarich_max_age_seconds: Ignore fixes older than this many seconds (60–86400). This is a quality filter, separate from the stale indicator.
data_description.dawarich_max_accuracy: Ignore fixes whose reported horizontal accuracy exceeds this many metres (1–10000). Lower values give more precise tracking but may skip indoor fixes.
data_description.dawarich_member: Optional exact Dawarich family email or user ID. Takes precedence over Person. Leave both empty to read the API key owner’s points. Family sharing must be enabled.
data_description.dawarich_person: Optional single Person for older servers matching its display name to a family name or email. Clear it for your own account; current servers should use the explicit member field.
data_description.dawarich_test_connection: Verify authentication and a usable location before saving. No data is uploaded. Leave off to save while the server is offline.
data_description.dawarich_verify_ssl: Verify the server TLS certificate. Keep off only for a trusted private server using a self-signed certificate; turning it on is recommended for public or properly certificated servers.
data_description.dawarich_request_timeout: Maximum seconds to wait for each API response (5–60). A timeout records a connection error and the next scheduled poll retries.
data_description.dawarich_include_visits: Fetch the latest visit separately after each successful own-account location poll. Turn off to reduce API calls; location and history still update.
data_description.dawarich_visit_lookback_days: How many days before the latest point to search for a visit (1–365). A longer period can require reading more visit pages.

local_presence_settings.name: Wi-Fi / BLE presence
local_presence_settings.description: Track selected devices through connection state and AB Gateway Bluetooth observations.

data_description.presence_enabled: Combine selected Wi-Fi connections and remote BLE observations with GPS. Disable and save to remove these local-presence settings.
data_description.presence_wifi_entities: Select router device trackers or connection binary sensors for the specific devices you want to track. For a Wi-Fi SSID sensor, also enter the exact home SSIDs below. Unavailable sources do not count as disconnected.
data_description.presence_wifi_ssids: One exact, case-sensitive SSID per line. Used only for selected sensor entities; any matching SSID means home. Do not enter Wi-Fi passwords.
data_description.presence_ble_addresses: One stable BLE MAC address per line. Only these devices are tracked; rotating private addresses require a stable identity supplied by another integration.
data_description.presence_ble_sources: One Home Assistant remote scanner source ID per line. AprilBrother component-ab-gateway uses ab_gateway by default. These are scanner source IDs, not MQTT topics or individual gateway MACs. Configure the gateway integration separately.
data_description.presence_ble_timeout: Seconds after the last qualifying advertisement before marking away (10–3600). Start around 90–180 seconds; increase it for sparse advertisements or weak coverage, decrease it only when you need faster away detection. Checked every 5 seconds; rereading cached advertisements never extends presence.
data_description.presence_ble_min_rssi: Only advertisements at or above this dBm level count as nearby (-127–0); values closer to 0 require a stronger signal. Start at -85 to -90 dBm, use about -70 to -80 dBm for room-level proximity, and lower it to -95 to -100 dBm for wider coverage. Walls, body blocking, phone orientation and gateway placement change RSSI, so calibrate from observed values; it is not a distance measurement.

entity_source.title: Copy From Existing Entities
entity_source.description: Optionally choose one or more Home Assistant entities. Multiple sources generate starter templates automatically.

data_description.reference_entity_id: Leave empty to create a virtual entity from scratch. Boolean sources use AND, motion/presence sources use majority with delayed clear, safety sources such as leak, smoke, gas, and water use OR, numeric sources use average, text sources use concat, date/time sources use latest, select sources use first available, and multiple location sources follow plausible GPS movement and keep the travelling device during stops. Without movement evidence they use median GPS with unconfirmed outlier priority (300 m for 30 minutes). A heating-only climate source is simplified to heat/off. Selecting exactly one climate and one switch creates a boiler helper: the hot-water switch remains on in both modes, heat uses the climate heat mode, and virtual off uses the climate fan-only mode. Camera and image sources can be aliased one at a time, not merged.
data_description.target_device_name: Choose an existing Virtual Device to keep its entities together, or create a new Device.
data_description.tracker_creation: Create a standard entity or open preconfigured Dawarich, Wi-Fi, or BLE tracker settings. Existing sources are optional. For Wi-Fi, select router trackers, connection sensors, or SSID sensors; for Dawarich/BLE, optional sources must be GPS trackers. Manage the created tracker through Edit/Delete Entity.

entity_type.description: Choose the type of virtual entity to create from this single source. Only source-to-target combinations with generated helper support are shown.

data_description.target_entity_type: The generated state, native-property, and supported command helpers will use this entity type. Multiple control and sensor sources can also compose one native virtual entity, such as a Humidifier.

sensor_conversion.title: Choose Sensor Measurement
sensor_conversion.description: Choose a measurement from control, air-quality, or sensor entities. Virtual Layer creates the value template, device class, state class, and unit automatically, and normalizes compatible particulate, gas, and radon units before combining sources.

data_description.sensor_conversion: Supports native values such as temperature, humidity, PM0.1, PM2.5, PM10, AQI, ozone, CO, CO2, SO2, NO, and NO2, plus radon and other existing sensor states.
data_description.sensor_aggregation: Average ignores unavailable and non-finite values and removes positive spikes above three times the median reference. Other modes ignore invalid values without removing valid extremes.

boiler_temperature_calibration.title: Boiler Temperature Adjustment
boiler_temperature_calibration.description: Choose this before source templates are generated. Direct setpoints are the default; enable conversion only when the boiler expects a water-temperature target rather than the room target.

data.boiler_temperature_calibration_enabled: Convert room target to water target

data_description.boiler_temperature_calibration_enabled: Off by default: send the requested temperature to the boiler unchanged. Turn it on only to generate and apply the room-to-water conversion formula.

entity_helper.title: Choose Template Generation
entity_helper.description: Choose whether to prefill the new virtual entity with Jinja templates generated from the selected source entities. You can review and customize all entity details and templates on the next screen.

data_description.use_template_helper: Turn this on to generate value, availability, icon, attribute, and domain-specific property templates. Turn it off to copy the source selection, current state, and metadata without generated templates.
data_description.boiler_temperature_calibration_template: Base conversion only: temperature * 1.5 + 2.5 (25°C room → 40°C water, 27°C → 43°C). This is not the dynamic formula. Its result is base_water_temperature in the feedback formula below. With feedback disabled it runs on temperature commands. Saved custom formulas are preserved.
data_description.boiler_temperature_calibration_enabled: Turn this off when the boiler accepts the same room target directly. The formula is retained for later use. Dynamic feedback then uses the room target as its base water temperature.
data_description.boiler_dynamic_control: Opt-in periodic feedback for one boiler climate source only; boiler + air-conditioner composite sources are not supported. Select room sensors on the next screen and use Celsius virtual units. Boiler current_temperature must measure water. This mode owns temperature writes; power/mode actions remain unchanged.
data_description.boiler_dynamic_template: Default includes room error, warming rate and residual heat. Variables: temperature (room target), room_temperature (sensor mean), boiler_water_temperature, room_temperature_rate (°C/min), heating_elapsed_minutes, heat_accumulation (decaying °C·min), base_water_temperature. Returns Celsius. When enabled, evaluates every 60 seconds; writes at least 120 seconds apart, limited to 2°C per change and boiler limits. Missing inputs pause writes. Tune gains for your system.

matter_fan_levels.description: This source exposes more than three speed steps. Choose which physical steps the generated helper will expose as low, medium, and high to Matter controllers.

data_description.matter_fan_medium_level: The source percentage used when a controller requests medium speed.

fan_source_roles.description: Choose the source used for each virtual-fan capability. Only sources that report support for a capability are offered. Leave an optional capability empty when no source should control it.

Start around 90–180 seconds; increase it for sparse advertisements or weak coverage, decrease it only when you need faster away detection. Checked every 5 seconds; rereading cached advertisements never extends presence.

Start at -85 to -90 dBm, use about -70 to -80 dBm for room-level proximity, and lower it to -95 to -100 dBm for wider coverage. Walls, body blocking, phone orientation and gateway placement change RSSI, so calibrate from observed values; it is not a distance measurement.

data_description.apply: Recommended. This changes this virtual sensor's value and unit templates only. It does not modify the source entity or stable entity ID. unit_change.title: Handle existing values after a unit change
unit_change.description:
Entity: {entity_id}. Saving normally changes the Virtual Entity unit from {old_unit} to {new_unit}. Recorded statistics currently use {statistics_unit}.

• Keep: Virtual Entity → {new_unit}; statistics numbers and unit stay unchanged.
• Restore: Virtual Entity → {statistics_unit}; the selected/template unit is replaced and statistics stay unchanged.
• Correct label: Virtual Entity and statistics unit → {new_unit}; numbers stay unchanged. Use only if historical numbers already use {new_unit}.
• Convert: Virtual Entity and statistics unit → {new_unit}; every recorded short- and long-term statistic number is converted.

Raw state history, current/restored values, templates, and thresholds never change. The saved Virtual Entity unit applies to future readings. '?' means the selected/template unit could not be resolved.

data.confirm_history: Confirm modification of all statistics for this entity

data_description.history_policy: Keep existing history: entity unit becomes the selected/template unit; statistics are untouched. Restore from statistics: entity unit becomes the normalized recorded unit; statistics are untouched. Correct label: entity and statistics units become the selected/template unit, without changing numbers. Convert: entity and statistics units become the selected/template unit, with Home Assistant converting statistic numbers. Restore is preselected when the selected/template unit is missing.
data_description.confirm_history: Required for correction or conversion. Applies to all recorded statistical periods, not a selected date range. Cancel the flow to leave the entity configuration unchanged.

Existing virtual sensors receive it on reload too. Original sensors are unchanged. A sensor.object_id_aqim compatibility mirror is also generated for matterbridge-hass 1.5.0; match that ID in the bridge's Air Quality Regex.

advanced_settings.description: Optional source mappings, attributes, event hooks, command actions, and integration-specific settings.

data_description.template_sources_json:
Maps Jinja variable names to source states or attributes. YAML example:
source: sensor.room_temperature
battery: sensor.remote.battery_level
Use variables named source and battery in editable templates.
Multiple sources:
source: sensor.room_temperature
battery: sensor.remote.battery_level
Then reference the variables from value_template.
data_description.event_hooks_json:
Runs editable helpers after a state or event trigger. YAML example:
- trigger: state
  entity_id: [sensor.source]
  value_template: trigger.to_state.state  # wrap in Jinja delimiters
Hooks may also set availability_template, attributes, and attribute_templates.
data_description.attributes_json:
Static extra attributes published by the virtual entity. YAML example:
source_type: composite
priority: 1
data_description.attribute_sources_json:
Maps a virtual attribute to a real entity state or attribute. YAML example:
battery: sensor.remote.battery_level
mode: select.real_mode.state
data_description.attribute_templates_json:
Maps attributes to editable Jinja helpers. YAML example:
power: states("sensor.power") | float(0)  # wrap this expression in Jinja delimiters
Automatic helpers use boolean AND/OR, numeric average, unique list union, string concatenation, or ordered mapping merge according to value type.
data_description.native_templates_json:
Maps native Home Assistant properties to Jinja. YAML example:
vendor_property: state_attr("sensor.source", "vendor_property")  # wrap in Jinja delimiters
Managed properties are normally shown individually in Native values; this editor keeps additional domain/vendor properties editable.
data_description.command_actions_json:
Maps every virtual-domain command to Home Assistant actions. Command arguments such as preset_mode, percentage, temperature, option, or position are template variables. YAML example:
set_preset_mode:
  - choose:
      - conditions: preset_mode == "sleep"  # wrap in Jinja delimiters
        sequence:
          - action: input_select.select_option
            target:
              entity_id: input_select.real_mode
            data:
              option: quiet
A value may be one action, an action list, or a mapping with sequence and optimistic keys.
More examples:
turn_on:
  - action: switch.turn_on
    target:
      entity_id: switch.real_device
set_percentage:
  - action: number.set_value
    target:
      entity_id: number.fan_speed
    data:
      value: percentage # command variable; wrap expressions in Jinja delimiters
data_description.domain_options_json:
Additional selected-domain options not represented by dedicated inputs. YAML example:
source_entity: camera.front_door
stream_source: rtsp://example/stream
Reserved common fields cannot be overridden.
Climate example:
hvac_modes: select.climate_modes
current_temperature: sensor.room_temperature
Fan example:
preset_modes: select.fan_modes
Use dedicated Native values for standard properties when available.

data_description.matter_light_type: Choose the maximum virtual-light capability: on/off, dimming, color temperature, or extended HS/XY color. When combining bulbs, the generated helper uses the least capable profile: RGB plus color-temperature becomes color temperature, and any on/off-only bulb makes the virtual light on/off only. Effects and flash are never exposed.
data_description.light_response_delay: Seconds to retain a requested light value before reading source states again (0–30).
data_description.light_response_retries: For light groups, refresh source devices and resend the latest command only to bulbs that have not reached the target (0–10 retries). A new command cancels old retries. Single-source lights only re-read state.
data_description.light_ignore_unresponsive: Keep the combined light available and use responding bulbs when another selected bulb is unavailable.
data_description.sensor_unit: Choose a normalized Home Assistant unit to replace the unit template. Keep template preserves dynamic or custom units. This does not convert readings.
data_description.boiler_dynamic_control: Opt in for one boiler and room sensors in Celsius. Replaces the configured set_temperature action with periodic water-temperature writes. Set a room target after enabling. Calculates every 60s; writes at least 120s apart. Boiler current_temperature must measure heating water. Power actions remain separately configured.
data_description.utility_meter_enabled: Accumulate one source sensor as a Utility Meter. This creates a period total and follows source increases; source resets are ignored.
data_description.boiler_dynamic_template: Returns Celsius. Variables: temperature (saved room target), room_temperature (sensor mean), boiler_water_temperature, room_temperature_rate (C/min over up to 10min), heating_elapsed_minutes (observed heat duration), heat_accumulation (decaying C-min proxy, 30min time constant), base_water_temperature (existing calibration result). Tune default gains for the system. Missing inputs pause writes. Boiler limits and steps apply.
data_description.boiler_room_temperature_entity_id: Optional sensors combined as the virtual climate's current room temperature. Available numeric readings are averaged; raw boiler-water temperatures remain available as attributes.
data_description.media_player_source_priority: Optional ordered fallback for the combined player. Drag sources into priority order. A playing, paused, or buffering source wins first; off, idle, unavailable, or unusable sources fall through. This shared order applies to all standard media-player properties.
data_description.onvif_patrol_enabled: Starts the patrol after this virtual camera loads. The video source remains independent from the PTZ target.
data_description.onvif_patrol_target: Select the camera created by Home Assistant's existing ONVIF integration. Its authenticated ONVIF client is also used if the PTZ action is unavailable.
data_description.onvif_patrol_mode: Legacy relative patrol only: horizontal alternates left/right, vertical down/up, grid both axes. A saved route from Configure camera patrol positions takes priority over these axes and ranges.
data_description.onvif_patrol_interval: Seconds to wait after each relative ONVIF move.
data_description.onvif_patrol_speed: Optional ONVIF speed coefficient, from 0 to 1.
data_description.onvif_patrol_pan_min: Relative move distance from 0 to 1 for each left movement.
data_description.onvif_patrol_pan_max: Relative move distance from 0 to 1 for each right movement.
data_description.onvif_patrol_tilt_min: Relative move distance from 0 to 1 for each down movement.
data_description.onvif_patrol_tilt_max: Relative move distance from 0 to 1 for each up movement.
data_description.patrol_auto_cycle: Start patrol on load, then repeat on/off periods. Manual patrol switch or service control suspends automatic cycles until reload.
data_description.patrol_on_seconds: How long each automatic patrol session runs. Default 300 seconds.
data_description.patrol_off_seconds: Time between the end of a session and the next start, after cleanup. Default 1800 seconds.
data_description.patrol_recording_scope: Apply recording policy for the entire patrol, or only during each movement including return. Between moves the previous state is restored.
data_description.patrol_settle_seconds: Wait this long after movement, then send ONVIF Stop before restoring recording. This is a timing estimate, not position feedback; increase for slower cameras.
data_description.frigate_recording_switch: Optional: select the Frigate recording switch. Otherwise controls are discovered on the source camera’s Frigate device. No other camera is controlled.
data_description.frigate_mqtt_recordings_topic: Base topic such as frigate/front/recordings. Also controls sibling detect and motion topics. Leave the switch empty. Requires state confirmation before movement.
data_description.frigate_recording_during_patrol: Off (default) disables recording during the selected control period. On enables it; Keep leaves it unchanged. Configure detection separately below. Stop restores the prior state.
data_description.frigate_motion_during_patrol: Controls both detect and motion. Off disables detection before motion; On enables motion before detection. Keep preserves both. Set both recording and detection to Off for quiet patrol.
data_description.configure_air_quality_rules: Automatically classify recognized PM1.0, PM2.5, PM4, PM10, radon, formaldehyde, CO2, CO, NO2, ozone, SO2, NO, N2O, benzene, ammonia, hydrogen sulfide and TVOC/eTVOC (mass or parts) measurements with separate starter profiles, then use the worst available grade. Source categories and AQI are also supported. Unsupported quantities or units remain unknown. Display bands are instantaneous, not official health standards or exposure-time assessments; good does not certify safe air. PM4 uses a labelled PM2.5-shaped display proxy; N2O uses local display bands, not occupational limits. Review/edit thresholds in the generated template or check for manual rules. Original sensors are unchanged.
data_description.air_quality_per_source: Keep the aggregate and original sensors; also create a categorical sensor for each source on this Device. Each uses its own automatic profile. Unsupported measurements remain unknown. Matterbridge Air Quality Regex and endpoint grouping must be configured separately.
data_description.configure_air_quality_sources: Keep the original sensor. Configure units, attributes, five boundaries, six grades and formulas for the combined measurement or each source. Unlike pollutants use the worst grade, never an average concentration.
data_description.polygon_catalog_ids: Select one or more shared areas from GeoJson Device Group. Register or edit GeoJSON in that group’s Configure menu.

data.dawarich_member: Family member email or user ID

data_description.dawarich_enabled: Enable polling for this tracker. Turn off to remove its saved Dawarich configuration.
data_description.dawarich_url: Base URL without /api/v1, for example https://dawarich.example.com.
data_description.dawarich_api_key: Stored in this integration configuration. The password field hides it on screen; it is not published in entity attributes.
data_description.dawarich_auth_mode: Use Bearer token or api_key query-parameter authentication.
data_description.dawarich_poll_interval: Seconds between API polls (15–3600). Point freshness uses its measurement timestamp, not poll time.
data_description.dawarich_history_limit: Maximum recent location summaries retained in dawarich_history (1–100). Family mode returns only the current location.
data_description.dawarich_max_age_seconds: Ignore fixes older than this many seconds (60–86400). This is a quality filter, separate from the stale indicator.
data_description.dawarich_max_accuracy: Ignore fixes whose reported horizontal accuracy exceeds this many metres (1–10000). Lower values give more precise tracking but may skip indoor fixes.
data_description.dawarich_member: Optional exact Dawarich family email or user ID. Takes precedence over Person. Leave both empty to read the API key owner’s points. Family sharing must be enabled.
data_description.dawarich_person: Optional single Person for older servers matching its display name to a family name or email. Clear it for your own account; current servers should use the explicit member field.
data_description.dawarich_test_connection: Verify authentication and a usable location before saving. No data is uploaded. Leave off to save while the server is offline.
data_description.dawarich_verify_ssl: Verify the server TLS certificate. Keep off only for a trusted private server using a self-signed certificate; turning it on is recommended for public or properly certificated servers.
data_description.dawarich_request_timeout: Maximum seconds to wait for each API response (5–60). A timeout records a connection error and the next scheduled poll retries.
data_description.dawarich_include_visits: Fetch the latest visit separately after each successful own-account location poll. Turn off to reduce API calls; location and history still update.
data_description.dawarich_visit_lookback_days: How many days before the latest point to search for a visit (1–365). A longer period can require reading more visit pages.

local_presence_settings.name: Wi-Fi / BLE presence
local_presence_settings.description: Track selected devices through connection state and AB Gateway Bluetooth observations.

data_description.presence_enabled: Combine selected Wi-Fi connections and remote BLE observations with GPS. Disable and save to remove these local-presence settings.
data_description.presence_wifi_entities: Select router device trackers or connection binary sensors for the specific devices you want to track. For a Wi-Fi SSID sensor, also enter the exact home SSIDs below. Unavailable sources do not count as disconnected.
data_description.presence_wifi_ssids: One exact, case-sensitive SSID per line. Used only for selected sensor entities; any matching SSID means home. Do not enter Wi-Fi passwords.
data_description.presence_ble_addresses: One stable BLE MAC address per line. Only these devices are tracked; rotating private addresses require a stable identity supplied by another integration.
data_description.presence_ble_sources: One Home Assistant remote scanner source ID per line. AprilBrother component-ab-gateway uses ab_gateway by default. These are scanner source IDs, not MQTT topics or individual gateway MACs. Configure the gateway integration separately.
data_description.presence_ble_timeout: Seconds after the last qualifying advertisement before marking away (10–3600). Start around 90–180 seconds; increase it for sparse advertisements or weak coverage, decrease it only when you need faster away detection. Checked every 5 seconds; rereading cached advertisements never extends presence.
data_description.presence_ble_min_rssi: Only advertisements at or above this dBm level count as nearby (-127–0); values closer to 0 require a stronger signal. Start at -85 to -90 dBm, use about -70 to -80 dBm for room-level proximity, and lower it to -95 to -100 dBm for wider coverage. Walls, body blocking, phone orientation and gateway placement change RSSI, so calibrate from observed values; it is not a distance measurement.

Existing virtual sensors receive it on reload too. Original sensors are unchanged. A sensor.object_id_aqim compatibility mirror is also generated for matterbridge-hass 1.5.0; match that ID in the bridge's Air Quality Regex.

advanced_settings.description: Optional source mappings, attributes, event hooks, command actions, and integration-specific settings.

data_description.template_sources_json:
Maps Jinja variable names to source states or attributes. YAML example:
source: sensor.room_temperature
battery: sensor.remote.battery_level
Use variables named source and battery in editable templates.
Multiple sources:
source: sensor.room_temperature
battery: sensor.remote.battery_level
Then reference the variables from value_template.
data_description.event_hooks_json:
Runs editable helpers after a state or event trigger. YAML example:
- trigger: state
  entity_id: [sensor.source]
  value_template: trigger.to_state.state  # wrap in Jinja delimiters
Hooks may also set availability_template, attributes, and attribute_templates.
data_description.attributes_json:
Static extra attributes published by the virtual entity. YAML example:
source_type: composite
priority: 1
data_description.attribute_sources_json:
Maps a virtual attribute to a real entity state or attribute. YAML example:
battery: sensor.remote.battery_level
mode: select.real_mode.state
data_description.attribute_templates_json:
Maps attributes to editable Jinja helpers. YAML example:
power: states("sensor.power") | float(0)  # wrap this expression in Jinja delimiters
Automatic helpers use boolean AND/OR, numeric average, unique list union, string concatenation, or ordered mapping merge according to value type.
data_description.native_templates_json:
Maps native Home Assistant properties to Jinja. YAML example:
vendor_property: state_attr("sensor.source", "vendor_property")  # wrap in Jinja delimiters
Managed properties are normally shown individually in Native values; this editor keeps additional domain/vendor properties editable.
data_description.command_actions_json:
Maps every virtual-domain command to Home Assistant actions. Command arguments such as preset_mode, percentage, temperature, option, or position are template variables. YAML example:
set_preset_mode:
  - choose:
      - conditions: preset_mode == "sleep"  # wrap in Jinja delimiters
        sequence:
          - action: input_select.select_option
            target:
              entity_id: input_select.real_mode
            data:
              option: quiet
A value may be one action, an action list, or a mapping with sequence and optimistic keys.
More examples:
turn_on:
  - action: switch.turn_on
    target:
      entity_id: switch.real_device
set_percentage:
  - action: number.set_value
    target:
      entity_id: number.fan_speed
    data:
      value: percentage # command variable; wrap expressions in Jinja delimiters
data_description.domain_options_json:
Additional selected-domain options not represented by dedicated inputs. YAML example:
source_entity: camera.front_door
stream_source: rtsp://example/stream
Reserved common fields cannot be overridden.
Climate example:
hvac_modes: select.climate_modes
current_temperature: sensor.room_temperature
Fan example:
preset_modes: select.fan_modes
Use dedicated Native values for standard properties when available.

data_description.polygon_geojson_json: Optional GeoJSON FeatureCollection containing named Polygon or MultiPolygon features. Used only by device_tracker entities.
data_description.polygon_files_text: One local path or HTTP(S) GeoJSON URL per line. Relative paths are resolved below the Home Assistant configuration directory.
data_description.polygon_person: Optional person represented by this virtual tracker. The configured source trackers determine the map position.
data_description.polygon_strategy: Adaptive follows observed movement, checks GPS accuracy and speed, and keeps the carried device during stops; stale positions are marked. Majority groups nearby trackers, priority selects the lowest rule priority, latest uses the newest update, and median combines all valid positions. Dominant rules override adaptive selection.

data_description.polygon_away_state: State used when the selected GPS position is outside every polygon.
data_description.presence_classification: Wi-Fi/ESPresense means home; BLE distance means front_door; GPS distance from zone.home becomes near_home, away, or far_away.
data_description.matter_light_type: Choose the maximum virtual-light capability: on/off, dimming, color temperature, or extended HS/XY color. When combining bulbs, the generated helper uses the least capable profile: RGB plus color-temperature becomes color temperature, and any on/off-only bulb makes the virtual light on/off only. Effects and flash are never exposed.
data_description.light_response_delay: Seconds to retain a requested light value before reading source states again (0–30).
data_description.light_response_retries: For light groups, refresh source devices and resend the latest command only to bulbs that have not reached the target (0–10 retries). A new command cancels old retries. Single-source lights only re-read state.
data_description.light_ignore_unresponsive: Keep the combined light available and use responding bulbs when another selected bulb is unavailable.
data_description.sensor_unit: Choose a normalized Home Assistant unit to replace the unit template. Keep template preserves dynamic or custom units. This does not convert readings.
data_description.boiler_dynamic_control: Opt in for one boiler and room sensors in Celsius. Replaces the configured set_temperature action with periodic water-temperature writes. Set a room target after enabling. Calculates every 60s; writes at least 120s apart. Boiler current_temperature must measure heating water. Power actions remain separately configured.
data_description.boiler_dynamic_template: Returns Celsius. Variables: temperature (saved room target), room_temperature (sensor mean), boiler_water_temperature, room_temperature_rate (C/min over up to 10min), heating_elapsed_minutes (observed heat duration), heat_accumulation (decaying C-min proxy, 30min time constant), base_water_temperature (existing calibration result). Tune default gains for the system. Missing inputs pause writes. Boiler limits and steps apply.
data_description.utility_meter_enabled: Accumulate one source sensor as a Utility Meter. This creates a period total and follows source increases; source resets are ignored.
data_description.boiler_room_temperature_entity_id: Optional sensors combined as the virtual climate's current room temperature. Available numeric readings are averaged; raw boiler-water temperatures remain available as attributes.
data_description.media_player_source_priority: Optional ordered fallback for the combined player. Drag sources into priority order. A playing, paused, or buffering source wins first; off, idle, unavailable, or unusable sources fall through. This shared order applies to all standard media-player properties.
data_description.onvif_patrol_enabled: Starts the patrol after this virtual camera loads. The video source remains independent from the PTZ target.
data_description.onvif_patrol_target: Select the camera created by Home Assistant's existing ONVIF integration. Its authenticated ONVIF client is also used if the PTZ action is unavailable.
data_description.onvif_patrol_mode: Legacy relative patrol only: horizontal alternates left/right, vertical down/up, grid both axes. A saved route from Configure camera patrol positions takes priority over these axes and ranges.
data_description.onvif_patrol_interval: Seconds to wait after each relative ONVIF move.
data_description.onvif_patrol_speed: Optional ONVIF speed coefficient, from 0 to 1.
data_description.onvif_patrol_pan_min: Relative move distance from 0 to 1 for each left movement.
data_description.onvif_patrol_pan_max: Relative move distance from 0 to 1 for each right movement.
data_description.onvif_patrol_tilt_min: Relative move distance from 0 to 1 for each down movement.
data_description.onvif_patrol_tilt_max: Relative move distance from 0 to 1 for each up movement.
data_description.patrol_auto_cycle: Start patrol on load, then repeat on/off periods. Manual patrol switch or service control suspends automatic cycles until reload.
data_description.patrol_on_seconds: How long each automatic patrol session runs. Default 300 seconds.
data_description.patrol_off_seconds: Time between the end of a session and the next start, after cleanup. Default 1800 seconds.
data_description.patrol_recording_scope: Apply recording policy for the entire patrol, or only during each movement including return. Between moves the previous state is restored.
data_description.patrol_settle_seconds: Wait this long after movement, then send ONVIF Stop before restoring recording. This is a timing estimate, not position feedback; increase for slower cameras.
data_description.frigate_recording_switch: Optional: select the Frigate recording switch. Otherwise controls are discovered on the source camera’s Frigate device. No other camera is controlled.
data_description.frigate_mqtt_recordings_topic: Base topic such as frigate/front/recordings. Also controls sibling detect and motion topics. Leave the switch empty. Requires state confirmation before movement.
data_description.frigate_recording_during_patrol: Off (default) disables recording during the selected control period. On enables it; Keep leaves it unchanged. Configure detection separately below. Stop restores the prior state.
data_description.frigate_motion_during_patrol: Controls both detect and motion. Off disables detection before motion; On enables motion before detection. Keep preserves both. Set both recording and detection to Off for quiet patrol.
data_description.configure_air_quality_rules: Automatically classify recognized PM1.0, PM2.5, PM4, PM10, radon, formaldehyde, CO2, CO, NO2, ozone, SO2, NO, N2O, benzene, ammonia, hydrogen sulfide and TVOC/eTVOC (mass or parts) measurements with separate starter profiles, then use the worst available grade. Source categories and AQI are also supported. Unsupported quantities or units remain unknown. Display bands are instantaneous, not official health standards or exposure-time assessments; good does not certify safe air. PM4 uses a labelled PM2.5-shaped display proxy; N2O uses local display bands, not occupational limits. Review/edit thresholds in the generated template or check for manual rules. Original sensors are unchanged.
data_description.air_quality_per_source: Keep the aggregate and original sensors; also create a categorical sensor for each source on this Device. Each uses its own automatic profile. Unsupported measurements remain unknown. Matterbridge Air Quality Regex and endpoint grouping must be configured separately.
data_description.configure_air_quality_sources: Keep the original sensor. Configure units, attributes, five boundaries, six grades and formulas for the combined measurement or each source. Unlike pollutants use the worst grade, never an average concentration.

dawarich_settings.description: Read location and history from Dawarich.

data.dawarich_member: Family member email or user ID

data_description.dawarich_enabled: Enable polling for this tracker. Turn off to remove its saved Dawarich configuration.
data_description.dawarich_url: Base URL without /api/v1, for example https://dawarich.example.com.
data_description.dawarich_api_key: Stored in this integration configuration. The password field hides it on screen; it is not published in entity attributes.
data_description.dawarich_auth_mode: Use Bearer token or api_key query-parameter authentication.
data_description.dawarich_poll_interval: Seconds between API polls (15–3600). Point freshness uses its measurement timestamp, not poll time.
data_description.dawarich_history_limit: Maximum recent location summaries retained in dawarich_history (1–100). Family mode returns only the current location.
data_description.dawarich_max_age_seconds: Ignore fixes older than this many seconds (60–86400). This is a quality filter, separate from the stale indicator.
data_description.dawarich_max_accuracy: Ignore fixes whose reported horizontal accuracy exceeds this many metres (1–10000). Lower values give more precise tracking but may skip indoor fixes.
data_description.dawarich_member: Optional exact Dawarich family email or user ID. Takes precedence over Person. Leave both empty to read the API key owner’s points. Family sharing must be enabled.
data_description.dawarich_person: Optional single Person for older servers matching its display name to a family name or email. Clear it for your own account; current servers should use the explicit member field.
data_description.dawarich_test_connection: Verify authentication and a usable location before saving. No data is uploaded. Leave off to save while the server is offline.
data_description.dawarich_verify_ssl: Verify the server TLS certificate. Keep off only for a trusted private server using a self-signed certificate; turning it on is recommended for public or properly certificated servers.
data_description.dawarich_request_timeout: Maximum seconds to wait for each API response (5–60). A timeout records a connection error and the next scheduled poll retries.
data_description.dawarich_include_visits: Fetch the latest visit separately after each successful own-account location poll. Turn off to reduce API calls; location and history still update.
data_description.dawarich_visit_lookback_days: How many days before the latest point to search for a visit (1–365). A longer period can require reading more visit pages.

local_presence_settings.name: Wi-Fi / BLE presence
local_presence_settings.description: Track selected devices through connection state and AB Gateway Bluetooth observations.

data_description.presence_enabled: Combine selected Wi-Fi connections and remote BLE observations with GPS. Disable and save to remove these local-presence settings.
data_description.presence_wifi_entities: Select router device trackers or connection binary sensors for the specific devices you want to track. For a Wi-Fi SSID sensor, also enter the exact home SSIDs below. Unavailable sources do not count as disconnected.
data_description.presence_wifi_ssids: One exact, case-sensitive SSID per line. Used only for selected sensor entities; any matching SSID means home. Do not enter Wi-Fi passwords.
data_description.presence_ble_addresses: One stable BLE MAC address per line. Only these devices are tracked; rotating private addresses require a stable identity supplied by another integration.
data_description.presence_ble_sources: One Home Assistant remote scanner source ID per line. AprilBrother component-ab-gateway uses ab_gateway by default. These are scanner source IDs, not MQTT topics or individual gateway MACs. Configure the gateway integration separately.
data_description.presence_ble_timeout: Seconds after the last qualifying advertisement before marking away (10–3600). Start around 90–180 seconds; increase it for sparse advertisements or weak coverage, decrease it only when you need faster away detection. Checked every 5 seconds; rereading cached advertisements never extends presence.
data_description.presence_ble_min_rssi: Only advertisements at or above this dBm level count as nearby (-127–0); values closer to 0 require a stronger signal. Start at -85 to -90 dBm, use about -70 to -80 dBm for room-level proximity, and lower it to -95 to -100 dBm for wider coverage. Walls, body blocking, phone orientation and gateway placement change RSSI, so calibrate from observed values; it is not a distance measurement.

entity_source.title: Copy From Existing Entities
entity_source.description: Optionally choose one or more Home Assistant entities. Multiple sources generate starter templates automatically.

data_description.reference_entity_id: Leave empty to create a virtual entity from scratch. Boolean sources use AND, motion/presence sources use majority with delayed clear, safety sources such as leak, smoke, gas, and water use OR, numeric sources use average, text sources use concat, date/time sources use latest, select sources use first available, and multiple location sources follow plausible GPS movement and keep the travelling device during stops. Without movement evidence they use median GPS with unconfirmed outlier priority (300 m for 30 minutes). A heating-only climate source is simplified to heat/off. data_description.tracker_creation: Create a standard entity or open preconfigured Dawarich, Wi-Fi, or BLE tracker settings. Existing sources are optional. data_description.aggregation: First valid selects the first usable category. Worst selects the most severe category after classifying each source. Applies to measurement mode only when classifying per source.
data_description.missing: Skip tries other valid sources; if none remain the result is unknown. Unknown requires every selected source to provide a valid value. Unavailable sources and invalid units count as missing.
data_description.grade_1: Category for interval 1. Repeated or reversed categories are allowed; interval 6 contains the largest values.
data_description.grade_2: Category for interval 2. Repeated or reversed categories are allowed; interval 6 contains the largest values.
data_description.grade_3: Category for interval 3. Repeated or reversed categories are allowed; interval 6 contains the largest values.
data_description.grade_4: Category for interval 4. Repeated or reversed categories are allowed; interval 6 contains the largest values.
data_description.grade_5: Category for interval 5. Repeated or reversed categories are allowed; interval 6 contains the largest values.
data_description.grade_6: Category for interval 6. Repeated or reversed categories are allowed; interval 6 contains the largest values.
data_description.quantity: Automatic uses known source device classes. Explicit selection treats mismatching state device_class as missing. Attributes use your declared quantity and unit. PM1 is not PM0.1.
data_description.reducer: Classify each source, or classify the mean, median, minimum or maximum of calibrated values once. Combine only the same physical quantity, never different pollutants.
data_description.boundary_rule: Upper inclusive: x ≤ boundary stays in the lower interval. Lower inclusive: x ≥ boundary enters the next interval.
data_description.quadratic: After unit conversion apply y = a×x² + b×x + c. Zero selects linear calibration. Negative or non-finite results count as missing.
data_description.multiplier: One preserves scale. Example: a=0, b=1.1, c=-2 yields y=1.1×x-2.
data_description.offset: Added after unit conversion and scaling. Zero leaves the offset unchanged.

air_quality_scope.title: Air-quality assessment scope

data_description.scope: Combined: the virtual sensor result. Sources: each selected sensor. Leaves: recursively expand configured Virtual Layer sources and deduplicate.

data_description.missing: Skip: assess valid sources only. Unknown: one unclassifiable source makes the overall grade unknown.

data.dawarich_member: Family member email or user ID

data_description.dawarich_enabled: Enable polling for this tracker. Turn off to remove its saved Dawarich configuration.
data_description.dawarich_url: Base URL without /api/v1, for example https://dawarich.example.com.
data_description.dawarich_api_key: Stored in this integration configuration. The password field hides it on screen; it is not published in entity attributes.
data_description.dawarich_auth_mode: Use Bearer token or api_key query-parameter authentication.
data_description.dawarich_poll_interval: Seconds between API polls (15–3600). Point freshness uses its measurement timestamp, not poll time.
data_description.dawarich_history_limit: Maximum recent location summaries retained in dawarich_history (1–100). Family mode returns only the current location.
data_description.dawarich_max_age_seconds: Ignore fixes older than this many seconds (60–86400). This is a quality filter, separate from the stale indicator.
data_description.dawarich_max_accuracy: Ignore fixes whose reported horizontal accuracy exceeds this many metres (1–10000). Lower values give more precise tracking but may skip indoor fixes.
data_description.dawarich_member: Optional exact Dawarich family email or user ID. Takes precedence over Person. Leave both empty to read the API key owner’s points. Family sharing must be enabled.
data_description.dawarich_person: Optional single Person for older servers matching its display name to a family name or email. Clear it for your own account; current servers should use the explicit member field.
data_description.dawarich_test_connection: Verify authentication and a usable location before saving. No data is uploaded. Leave off to save while the server is offline.
data_description.dawarich_verify_ssl: Verify the server TLS certificate. Keep off only for a trusted private server using a self-signed certificate; turning it on is recommended for public or properly certificated servers.
data_description.dawarich_request_timeout: Maximum seconds to wait for each API response (5–60). A timeout records a connection error and the next scheduled poll retries.
data_description.dawarich_include_visits: Fetch the latest visit separately after each successful own-account location poll. Turn off to reduce API calls; location and history still update.
data_description.dawarich_visit_lookback_days: How many days before the latest point to search for a visit (1–365). A longer period can require reading more visit pages.

local_presence_settings.name: Wi-Fi / BLE presence
local_presence_settings.description: Track selected devices through connection state and AB Gateway Bluetooth observations.

data_description.presence_enabled: Combine selected Wi-Fi connections and remote BLE observations with GPS. Disable and save to remove these local-presence settings.
data_description.presence_wifi_entities: Select router device trackers or connection binary sensors for the specific devices you want to track. For a Wi-Fi SSID sensor, also enter the exact home SSIDs below. Unavailable sources do not count as disconnected.
data_description.presence_wifi_ssids: One exact, case-sensitive SSID per line. Used only for selected sensor entities; any matching SSID means home. Do not enter Wi-Fi passwords.
data_description.presence_ble_addresses: One stable BLE MAC address per line. Only these devices are tracked; rotating private addresses require a stable identity supplied by another integration.
data_description.presence_ble_sources: One Home Assistant remote scanner source ID per line. AprilBrother component-ab-gateway uses ab_gateway by default. These are scanner source IDs, not MQTT topics or individual gateway MACs. Configure the gateway integration separately.
data_description.presence_ble_timeout: Seconds after the last qualifying advertisement before marking away (10–3600). Start around 90–180 seconds; increase it for sparse advertisements or weak coverage, decrease it only when you need faster away detection. Checked every 5 seconds; rereading cached advertisements never extends presence.
data_description.presence_ble_min_rssi: Only advertisements at or above this dBm level count as nearby (-127–0); values closer to 0 require a stronger signal. Start at -85 to -90 dBm, use about -70 to -80 dBm for room-level proximity, and lower it to -95 to -100 dBm for wider coverage. Walls, body blocking, phone orientation and gateway placement change RSSI, so calibrate from observed values; it is not a distance measurement.

data_description.utility_meter_enabled: Accumulate one source sensor as a Utility Meter. This creates a period total and follows source increases; source resets are ignored.
data_description.back: Keep the draft and return without saving.
data_description.utility_meter_cycle: Changing the cycle or dates retains the running total and schedules future resets from the edit onward. Use the reset action to start at zero.
data_description.utility_meter_start: ISO date/time, e.g. 2026-01-15T00:00:00. Local HA time unless an offset is supplied. Day 31 clamps to month end.
data_description.utility_meter_days: Calendar days from the start date; used for the N-day cycle.
data_description.utility_meter_offset: Shift the calendar anchor by 0–40319 minutes. Ignored for cron.
data_description.utility_meter_cron: Five-field cron in Home Assistant local time; used only for cron cycle.
data_description.utility_meter_delta_values: Add each new source event as consumption rather than subtracting cumulative readings.
data_description.utility_meter_net_consumption: Allow negative deltas for import/export meters; publishes total statistics.
data_description.utility_meter_periodically_resetting: Discard the baseline across invalid source states. Disable for a lifetime counter to bridge outages.
data_description.utility_meter_always_available: Retain the accumulated total when the source is unavailable.
data_description.utility_meter_tariff_entity: Optional select/input_select entity; create one meter per tariff on this Device.
data_description.utility_meter_tariff: Collect only while the tariff selector matches this exact option. Automations can switch the selector by time.
data_description.utility_meter_rate: Price per source unit, also above the final tier. Editing prices recalculates the entire current-period estimate, not historical price segments.
data_description.utility_meter_base_charge: Fixed charge per period. For multiple tariff meters, charge the base on one meter only.
data_description.utility_meter_currency: Three-letter currency code such as KRW or USD.
data_description.utility_meter_tiers: List of objects with up_to and rate keys and increasing cumulative limits. Empty uses the unit price.
data_description.utility_meter_current_value: Audited absolute total, applied once on save with a new source baseline. Leave blank to retain the total, including when changing the schedule. If offline, the first recovered reading becomes the baseline.
data_description.utility_meter_compare_previous_month: Reads the same local date and time one month earlier, refreshed every minute. Requires a month of Recorder state history (35-day retention recommended). Missing history or a changed unit reports unknown.
